#3976. Don't be fooled by Horses of Hoofprint Bay's hand-drawn art, this stable management game has all the drama of a Jilly Cooper novel

Poema is my pride and joy. She was my first horse and she's a competition winner, but she's reached her potential. She'll never be a show jumper, and that's where the money and prestige are to be found. If I'm ever to grow my horse farm into a nationally renowned equestrian centre, I need the cash to expand and upgrade my facilities. Poema is a hoofstep on the path to that future, but she's not going to be able to take me all the way herself.

For all its hand-drawn aesthetics, Horses of Hoofprint Bay has hard realities like the limits of Poema's future bubbling under its surface. While the game's scripted narrative may be lacking, it's shockingly easy to fill in the gaps with drama worthy of a Jilly Cooper novel.

There may be better author comparisons, but I learned everything I know about showjumping from Cooper's Riders – much as I learned everything about independent television franchise bids in the '80s from its sequel Rivals – a book which is as much about the nitty gritty of horsetraining and competing as it is about toffs jumping into bed with one another. In my mind the two are tightly connected - showjumping and Jilly Cooper, not horses and toff bonking. In Horses of Hoofprint Bay, the only real story you get is the fact you've scrimped and saved to buy your first horse and your uncle has lent you the use of his field while you start your business. I was hoping there would at least be a similar setup to Regency Solitaire, where your motivation for touring the country's tearooms is motivated by paying off your brother's gambling debts. Yet, despite this disappointing start, I soon found its business simulation mechanics provide great storytelling material.

Horses of Hoofprint Bay has many of the trappings of a cosy game. At the start of each day, you'll prepare the stables, dragging a rake around the yard to sling away the manure, clicking buckets of water to refill the trough, and making sure there's enough hay for all the horses. But this isn't just for the larks, if you skip these tasks there are serious knock on effects for yours horses. Forget to brush down your horses' coats or pick out the stones in their shoes, and they're liable to develop saddle sores and other injuries when you ride them. Leave an abrasion untreated and it can develop into an infection. Even something like taking a dirty horse to a contest can cost you. I forgot to brush Poema before entering her into her first contest and despite taking first place, her embarrassingly unkempt coat lost my stable prestige. It was a cruel end to what should have been a great celebration.

So long as your horses are well rested, you can train them each day. You may want to take them through some confidence building lunges, where they need to walk, trot, and canter on demand, or a more physically demanding Cavaletti or showjumping course. These latter too are much more tiring, but they build a horse's strength and endurance. The higher its endurance the more energy it can expend on training sessions each day, and the higher its strength the more jumps it can do in succession before slowing to a walk for a breather - essential when you're competing in a timed competition. Overdo the exercise, however, and you'll exhaust a horse, severely reducing its energy for the next day.

Now, unlike Poema, my freshly bought stallion Kolizey has the potential to compete in showjumping competitions. He'll never go all the way to the big national contests, but he can take a ribbon in the district and regional contests. Or he will when he's up to standard; he's arrived from the breeder in a sorry state: brambles in his mane, mud on his flanks, stones in his shoes, and his strength and endurance are far too low to make it through an entire course of obstacles.

The biggest problem, however, is Kolizey's confidence: it's shot. I don't know what was happening in the stalls at the breeder's, but he arrived at my stables backing up at the first sign of a jump. Before I can hope to earn him his first ribbon, I have to build up our relationship. If we exercise together enough in the yard, his confidence will grow and he will follow my direction without question.

It may be getting ahead of myself, but I also have plans for Kolizey and Poema to produce a foal. Done right, the two should raise a horse that's able to exceed its parents' potential, becoming stronger and more endurant than both of them. A stronger horse means a ticket to the bigger contests and the bigger prize pots. Not that I can start breeding the two just yet. I want both horses to be at peak physical fitness. Poema's already there, while Kolizey can't even manage a jump without shying away.

While getting Koliszey contest ready, I still need to be bringing in cash. That means using Poema as a training horse for students' riding lessons. The better I am at the minigame where I use the Q, E, W, A, S, and D keys to tell them to sit forward or back, hold the reins higher or lower, or to level out their legs, the more they tip me. I have to be careful, because when Poema is working with students, she's not being stretched, and her strength and endurance can wither which means she struggles to maintain her winning streak in the contests.

Another reason to hold off on getting Poema pregnant is that during the second half of her pregnancy, she can't be ridden, which means no contests and no lessons for students. Currently, those are my two main sources of income besides what I'm paid in rent to board a couple of nearby farmers' horses. I don't want her out of the rota when Kolizey isn't yet ready to step into her place.

And, well, while I'm on the subject of plans, reader, I must tell you, the future lies in semen. If I can build the facilities, earn the cash, and raise Kolizey's profile, I can make a good buck on his virile stallion cream. With the money I bring in from a prizewinning semen I can expand into the far field, creating space to take on more horses, upgrade my home from the caravan I'm living in currently, maybe even build a proper training school. I'm not going to afford all that by giving riding lessons to the local children or boarders' rent. No, the big money comes from competition wins and valuable horse sauce.

While Poema continues entering contests and carrying students, I start pushing Kolizey harder. Multiple training sessions every day. I begin with Cavaletti, which is a kind of obedience competition. Your horse has to be travelling at the correct speed when it passes marker flags – walking, trotting, or cantering – and make some small jumps over cross bars. It should be straightforward, but because Kolizey's confidence is so low, he keeps refusing my orders and trying to change speed. He warns me before he's about to speed up or slow down, and if I counter it in time he will obey me and even receive a little confidence boost, but often he does it just before a jump, messing up my timing and he hits the bars. Each time he fails a jump it knocks his confidence, risking me taking me even further from where I need him to be.

I try the easier lunges sessions. And they raise his confidence a little but they're doing little for his physical health. It's all taking too long and Poema's getting older every day. In a fit of frustration, and in mark that I may not be able to cut it as an animal trainer, I skip from the Cavaletti training straight into a showjumping qualifier. The time limits on these are much stricter, so you have to clear the course at a gallop. This is also where a horse's strength really comes into play. The faster you're going, the more strength it requires to jump an obstacle. Horses only recover strength when moving at a walk, so you don't want to tire a horse out by going at a gallop through the whole course, else they won't have the strength to make all the jumps and they'll be forced to withdraw from the event. But nor do you want to go too slowly and fall foul of the time limit.

I realise my mistake as soon as the course begins: I try to stir Kolizey into a walk he refuses. Thankfully the timer only starts when he crosses the line, but it's an inauspicious start. I tap forward again and he begins to walk. I tap again and Kolizey moves up to a trot, then to a canter, before picking up to a gallop. I think he's going too fast as we approach the first jump, but Kolizey clears it. Then another jump and another. With a nervous eye on the depleting strength bar, I tap him down to a canter for the next jump. We're halfway through the course, I briefly slow to a walk to recover some strength then take the next three jumps at a canter. We're so close to the end now but a big yellow exclamation mark appears next to the strength bar. Kolizey is on the edge of exhaustion but he refuses to slow down and increases to a gallop for the last two jumps.

He completes the course with a perfect clear. Not a single obstacle clipped and we end with ten seconds left on the timer. Not only has Kolizey earned his showjumping license, his success swells his confidence. He's a natural athlete.

The next day, with my horses rested, I take Kolizey and Poema to town to compete in the showjumping and Caprilli events respectively. They both bring home first place, raising the prestige of my stables, earning me a tidy little packet, and convincing me it's time my prized horses started a family. I'm perhaps too eager, when I try to send them to the breeding station, I'm told they're both 'Done for the day'. I suppose I should give my contest winners a bit of a break. They've earned it. I groom them and send them both to bed with an apple as a treat.

Except, maybe they weren't too tired: the next morning, I'm met with a message telling me Poema is pregnant. My stable's become the Olympic Village, with my rosette-winning horses working out the highs and stresses of competition in the only way they know how. Good on them. I needn't have even made the breeding station.

Then, with horror, I remember the horses I'm boarding for the neighbours. They're both stallions themselves. Neither of them are at competition level, their strength and endurance is lower even than Poema's when she arrived at the stable. If either of them are the father, Poema is about to be out of action for a whole season and at the other end of it I'll have a foal that can't even compete in the beginner events. fetch the equestrian version of Hercule Poirot, I need to find out who impregnated my horse!

It may not be a plot worthy of Cooper, but it will do for me.

#3975. Talking Point: What Are You Playing This Weekend? (14th November)

Well folks, you've made it through another week – well done! Chances are many of you have completed your quest in Ocarina of Time by now, with many more of you eagerly awaiting your next jaunt across Leonida when GTA 6 launches on the 19th.

Going back to OoT for a moment, Nintendo confirmed this week that it managed to sell over 5 million copies in just 4 days – astonishing! The company also revealed some behind-the-scenes info about the ReDead enemies, while we took at look at what we think are some of the best 'tiny tweaks' in the remake.

Elsewhere, Nintendo announced it will be ceasing Apple and Google sign-ins on Nintendo Accounts, while the Switch 2 received yet another system update.

Reviews this week include Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy (7/10), Queen's Domain (9/10), Metaphor ReFantazio (8/10), and Harold Halibut (7/10).

Talking Point With Big Walk, The AI-In-Game-Dev Debate Just Got A Lot Murkier

Talking Point What's Your Favourite Tiny Tweak In Zelda: Ocarina Of Time?

I had plans to possibly play the Xbox or PS5 Pro this weekend (they’ve been neglected) but it seems like I have bigger fish to fry on my Switch 2! I played majority of Harold Halibut this week for the review and I’m so close to the end. It’s only right I should finish it yeah?

Once that’s ticked off the backlog, I have more progress to make in Final Fantasy Resonance and I might even dare to play OoT more if I have the time. No doubt something will spoil my plans so my backup might be a Peak session with my pals.

Not the best of weekends for city integrity because both Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered and Earth Defense Force 5 continue to delight my free time. I am still hooked on Tape to Tape with a few teams left to unlock. I made the mistake of buying Warhammer Survivors and I fear the combination of 40k/Age of Sigmar lore with the Vampire Survivors addictive game loop will be the downfall of my productivity elsewhere. On the 16-bit retro-front I got Legend of Galactic Heroes on the Super Famicom. This has been on my bucket list for decades, and I'm glad to report the game lives up to the brilliant source material.

Game of the week is The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Everyone has probably completed the game by now, but I am still on the way to Zora’s Domain. I was there, Gandalf, 28 years ago when the original released on N64, thus I know what to do and where to go to, quickly breezing through the game like the Star Fox reboot. I am slowly enjoying the journey, a bit jealous for all the players experiencing this journey for the first time. Dare I dream for F-Zero X to get similar love next year?

Queen's Domain has got me royally hooked. After a somewhat confusing and frustrating start, I'm now deep into the game in all but actual progression, and its classic PC stylings and game design are just ticking so many boxes I'd forgotten I had.

It's still frustrating, but lord help me am I going to push on through this weekend.

So I played Alone in the Dark last weekend, as promised. It's not great. However, Queen's Domain is great, so I definitely plan to put a bit more time into it over the next few days or so.

Despite the very minor upgrades, I'm also keen to dive into Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy. The visuals have definitely received a nice bump in quality, so it'll be nice to experience the campaign in glorious 4K.

I have other games that I want to squeeze in before 2026 is up, but I simply haven't been able to pry myself away from Ocarina of Time yet. I was so unsure about it from the initial reveal, but goodness me, I love this remake so much.

Despite my best efforts to stretch it out for as long as possible, I only have a few dungeons to go at this point. I'm going to be a wreck at the finale.

The kids and I are heading up Death Mountain this weekend, although by the time you read this we’ve probably already done in Dodongo and are beansing it to Zora’s Domain.

Unfortunately, playing through Ocarina my spawn means that I can’t continue once they’ve gone to bed. And yet despite having dozens of 2026's finest to be getting on with (finished Mixtape this week, great stuff), I’m stuck in a very enjoyable COD funk, with all sorts of numbers in multiplayer. Have a good one, folks.

Those are our plans, but what about yours? Let us know what you'll be slapping in your Switch (2) in the poll below.

Nintendo Life’s resident horror fanatic, when he’s not knee-deep in Resident Evil and Silent Hill lore, Ollie likes to dive into a good horror book while nursing a lovely cup of tea. He also enjoys long walks and listens to everything from TOOL to Chuck Berry.

Well, after last week’s rather unfortunate timing of my daughter falling ill on the very day Ocarina of Time launched, I’m delighted to report she’s made a full recovery and has officially started nursery! A big week of milestones in our household, both in Hyrule and the real world.

As for Link, things have escalated rather dramatically. I met a lovely sage who kindly aged me seven years, returned to Castle Town to find the neighbourhood had gone downhill somewhat, and encountered a deeply unsettling graveyard child with a worrying obsession with skull masks.

Since then, I’ve managed to keep pace with the restless soul of Dampé, who rewarded my efforts with a shiny new Hookshot, and I’m now knee deep in the Forest Temple. I’ve also accidentally consumed an alarming number of poes. Don’t ask.

I’m hoping to keep up a steady pace of a temple or two a week from here, all while enjoying the build-up to a very special Christmas as my beautiful daughter approaches her first birthday. Watching her discover the world while I rediscover Hyrule feels rather fitting, really.

Tonight I'm not seeing my friends so I'll just continue with my schedule:

Ultros: starting my 3rd time-loop, really curious how this will go and hoping I'm not heading to a dead-end XD

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort: been playing Island Crown at Tennis and Bowling, and unlocking all sorts of queer items 🤭. Ah, that good old Wii Sports! 😍

Tetris Effect: Connected: participating in the weekend ritual, as usual ...

And SMB Wonder, RP Groove and MK World will be the three multiplayer contenders...

Have fun, happy gaming, and make the most of your weekend! ✌🏻🧡🎮

Sonic Generations: The 3DS version, specifically. It's absolutely terrible. I've played a lot of bad Sonic games, but this is something else. I'm currently at the final boss and I feel like I've sunk into the centre of the Triceratops poop in Jurassic Park. The controls just don't make sense; sometimes they behave exactly as they should, while sometimes they literally do the exact opposite of what I've pressed. I don't know if I'll finish this game, but I do know that if I don't finish it then I won't lose sleep over it.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (2026): I rolled credits on this last night and… wow. No game is truly perfect but, as a remake, this is perfect. Faithful yet tweaked where you'd want it to be, and utterly gorgeous on top. It feels weird to say that a 2026 remake of a 1998 game is my game of the year so far and worth buying a Switch 2 for, but Ocarina of Time is my game of the year so far and worth buying a Switch 2 for.

Professor Layton and the Curious Village: I'm still chipping away at this; a few puzzles here, a few puzzles there. Will I ever finish it? Who knows? Does it still make me feel like a dullard incredibly frequently? Yes.

Super Mario 3D Land and New Super Mario Bros. 2: There are still secret exits and star coins to find, and I will find them all!

Additionally, even though I've played through Ocarina of Time, Skyward Sword HD and Tears of the Kingdom over the past few months, I'm already hankering for more Zelda. I'm torn between A Link Between Worlds, or either of Oracle of Ages/Oracle of Seasons. I've not played any of them before. Or maybe I do yet another playthrough of The Minish Cap? 👀

I’ve also accidentally consumed an alarming number of poes. Don’t ask.

This weekend I will be working towards the endgame of Final Fantasy Resonance. Just reached the big reveal of Umbra's identity which I guessed ages ago but despite some predictability in the narrative I still think the writing is really strong and I'm connecting with the characters in a way I have with the best Final Fantasy games prior.

Will also put more time into the excellent Queen's Domain. The game is really starting to open up now that I have evolved a weapon and bested the first boss netting the big game changer traversal reward for that accomplishment. Still have to play with the utmost caution but I love the game so far.

Finally more Street Fighter 6 and Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered with the kids. At the request of my son we'll also put more time into Super Smash Bros. Ultimate. I hadn't played in years so he stomped me the first few rounds but my muscle memory kicked in and I sent him packing to Kingdom Hearts with Sora.

More OOT of course 👍 Still only in the early game as Ive had a lot on, in and out of work. Equally, I dont want to rush the experience as every moment I am thoroughly enjoying.

Im in the market for another CRT so might do some hunting for one to add to my retro setup.

Rest of the weekend, probably some Burnout Takedown. 170+ events in the game and Im trying to get gold in each.

Well, this was quite a week in terms of reducing and expanding the backlogs. I'm finally through with Nonograms Prophecy...at least with what I could access of it because the last two Big Picture slots still say "in progress" while solving everything else in the mode still left the counter at 0/10 (a remarkable counter in itself because there are 9 big pictures without the unplayable tutorial as is, 11 with the missing stuff and 12 if you do count the tutorial). Might be DLC stuff but the page shows no signs of the latter, and honestly? After 40 hours, I think I'm good.😄

I've also finally wrapped up Wolfenstein: The New Order and dipped my toes into The Old Blood, but The New Colossus is more of a priority now. Where to install it, though? Ah, that's a whole other story. The 512 Gb Express SanDisk gambled with at a regional online marketplace (after the only Minsk retailer previously stocking it messaged me back about not getting any more stuff shipped in) arrived last Sunday night, getting properly recognized by the console right on pickup... then repeatedly heating up and autoejected in the laptop beyond 4 Gb of data (from the backups to avoid redownloading). I had done enough reading about online marketplace fakes and their proverbial real capacity that my immediate reactions defy sharing here in public, but tested the thing in Switch 2 again... and it does work there?🤔 Everything from the previously installed stuff to the newly added FFXIV trial and the retrieved Gamecube app downloaded and proceeded to run without a hitch. Knocking on wood here, but the bullet may have been ultimately dodged.

Anyhoo, the Gen 10 storage expansion with roughly 80 Gb left of it even urged me to pull the trigger on the juicy FFVIIR discounts after all, although both games are 10 Gb bigger, unlikely to get completed before Xenoblade 3's bloa- er, upgraded filesize arrives (not to mention next year's Genesis) and still probably best benched at least until I finish Crisis Core. What did get installed from the spoils of the same eShop top-up is Drop Duchy and Souldiers, if at the expense of Vampire Hunters on OLED. What? New Colossus? Right - so the aforementioned 256 Gb card became predictably vacant and I'm still too unenthused about last gen's period of juggling multiple cards per console (what with repeatedly powering on and off in the process) to use it properly, so I really just went and boosted Mariko's storage towards many a previously shelved playthrough instead. New Colossus and Biomutant, Haven and Snake Pass, Layers of Fear 2 and Mad Rat Dead, Immortals and Starlink, Amalur and Dragon's Dogma, Outer Worlds and Pillars of Eternity, Astral Chain and Nocturne, Nelke and WoFF, Diablo 2 and Rebel Galaxy Outlaw, Red Dead Redemption and Devil Ma- never mind, the last one promptly got kicked back out to accommodate New Colossus last night. No, no room left to immediately reinstall Vampire Hunters but you can't win them all.

Needless to say, the weekend's hybrid appetites are encompassing the whole list above alongside the OLED's (Ball x Pit, Drop Duchy, KH1, Eternia, Yumia, Potion Permit, DerQ, and AC2) and NS2's (Motorfest, RE4, FFXIV, Cyberpunk, Tales of Arise, XC2 and Factorio) respective troves. Barely even making plans for the handhelds as a result, although some Flotsam, Xenosaga, Gravity Rush and Chase Begins may still show up on the menu. And that's enough of my first world pseudoblog.😅

Me and my 5 year old weean have been playing Pikmin 4 this past month.

Now the upgrade is here he’s been absolutely delighted to order Oachi about and it’s actually helping pronunciation of his second language cos Oachi’s a finicky bugger at times.

In fact, much like my son, Oachi seems to have very selective hearing and doesn’t take well to commands but picks up even the faintest, mumbled utterance of praise. I’ll say ‘good job’ as my son herds his Pikmin away from a boss attack only for Oachi to stop in his tracks as his senseless spaceman jockey pats him on the head as masses of Pikmin fall to a follow up attack. Then my son gets upset.

The game looks completely beautiful since the upgrade and the people refusing to buy it at 30fps are missing Nintendo at their artistic and creative zenith. Stunning game in every sense - I walked over a small patch of tin foil this afternoon and of course Nintendo recorded specific footsteps for it.

Seeing my son recall character names better than me and watching him judder as something creepy crawly pops into view has been priceless. Cherished time.

Asha Sharma says MachineGames "has done remarkable work" on Wolfenstein

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Wolfenstein 3 is officially in the works at MachineGames, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has announced.

Sharma has been firing off semi-big announcements via her official Twitter account all day in celebration of Xbox's 25th anniversary, including confirmation that Id Software is working on a new game, but this is undoubtedly the biggest news of the bunch.

"Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at @MachineGames," reads a tweet from Sharma. "One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more."

Not much else was revealed about the Wolfenstein revival, but it's exciting to know it's a full-blown mainline entry and not a spinoff ala Young Blood (which I enjoyed, to be fair). This will be the first mainline entry in the legendary first-person shooter series since 2017's Wolfenstein 2: The New Colossus, which somehow was almost 10 years ago.

Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at @MachineGames. One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more. https://t.co/YyX8LrbTvhNovember 12, 2026

Remember when I said "not much else was revealed" about Wolfenstein 3? Well, that's because Sharma was generous enough to tease us with a picture appearing to show the first page of Wolfenstein 3's dialogue script, seemingly confirming the first chapter is called Nazitraz. The scene opens in the inside of an interrogation cell with a conversation between longtime Wolfenstein protagonist William Joseph "B.J." Blazkowicz and a German-speaking character called Otto, which could be a number of bad guys throughout Wolfenstein history. B.J.'s longtime right hand, Fergus, also seems to be in the scene, but that's about everything that can be inferred based on what's shown.

MachineGames has been Bethesda's trusted Wolfenstein developer since 2014, starting with Wolfenstein: The New Order.

No details regarding platforms or release timing were revealed.

#3973. Mini Review: Shrek 2 Remastered (PS5) - Far Far Away Gets an All-Star Makeover

I believe, I believe, I believe this is a good time

Version Reviewed: PS5 (Standard) / European

While DreamWorks' tales of an ogre and his mates are hit or miss, there's no denying that Shrek 2 Remastered is a winning overhaul of a mid-2000s gem.

It comes from an era when movie tie-in games were all the rage, whether that meant half-arsed Harry Potter adventures or excellent efforts like X-Men Origins: Wolverine.

Shrek 2 is a thoroughly joyous time, adopting a Marvel Ultimate Alliance-style formula for its antics. Shrek, Fiona, and Donkey form the core team you'll swap between, with familiar faces like Lil Red and the Gingerbread Man joining the squad from time to time.

Each character packs special abilities, whether that's Donkey's 'Burro Blast' or Fiona's power to slow down time, Matrix-style. It's incredibly silly, and never commented on by our delightful cast. We wouldn't have it any other way.

Across a variety of locales from the titular movie, you'll squash, splatter, and swashbuckle through puzzles that take advantage of everyone's unique abilities.

Whether that's using Shrek's strength to hurl chickens into a pen for a fast food chain, or Donkey's agility to sneak up on a goblin that poops gems in a museum, there's plenty of variety.

'Hero Time' moments also spice things up, ranging from QTEs involving Fiona singing (badly) to birds, to Donkey riding Elizabeth the Dragon in a fiery chase.

There's more depth here than your usual movie game slop, too, with friendly leprechaun Crazy Larry selling stat increases and upgrades in exchange for your hard-earned coins. It scratches that familiar LEGO game itch of smashing objects, platforming, and exploring every nook and cranny for collectibles.

All of it looks and sounds the part, with a faithful recreation of DreamWorks' fantastical art direction and an appropriately over-the-top score.

Where Shrek 2 Remastered really comes together is its brand-new co-op multiplayer. Played locally or online, the latter requiring an Epic Games Account, you can team up with three other players. It's a neat inclusion for a game that's over two decades old.

There's also a basic but enjoyable Photo Mode, perfect for capturing some amusing shots of the gang.

Performance on base PS5 is generally stable, although frame drops occasionally rear their ugly heads during crowded skirmishes or when loading new areas. Paired with an occasionally awkward camera, these blemishes don't hurt the experience too much.

Shrek 2 Remastered doesn't quite polish away all the rough edges of its original release, but there's so much charm here that it's difficult to hold them against it.

With a varied adventure, plenty of laughs, and the welcome addition of online co-op, this is a lovely reminder of when movie tie-in games could be just as entertaining as the films that inspired them.

#3972. Big Walk developer House House reveal genAI use in final stretch of development, only revealing it now as "it has become a matter of public interest"

Friendslop du jour Big Walk is the latest in an unfortunately long series of games that have been confirmed to use generative AI in their production, with developers House House clarifying their use of it in a statement to Aftermath (thanks!). House House state that "LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs", and that "well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code had anything to do with this usage", but are quick to note that "generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game."

A specific example is given in the case of Unity's apparent weirdness around shadow casters in its rendering pipeline, as it's seemingly difficult to have unnecessary shadow casters behind the player culled, which resulted in the game running at half speed around sunrise and sunset. House House explain that they couldn't find a solution themselves, asked a Unity engineer for help who said it was impossible, and then decided the only answer was to ask an LLM chatbot; "after a few dead ends, it suggested a possible fix, and while we had to modify the suggestion extensively, it worked. This fix represented about 10 lines of code." While absolutely not the most pressing thing to mention here, it is very funny to me for House House to clarify that they "had to modify the suggestion extensively", almost as if this tech isn't actually helpful in giving useful answers.

So, House House touched the stove, despite how easy it is to simply not touch the stove. The thing is, this wasn't a case of being forced to by upper management, as is sometimes the case. This was a choice made entirely voluntarily, and House House are attempting to have their cake and eat it by ending their statement with the reflection that "We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as “inevitable”. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologise that Big Walk’s LLM usage may not meet their standards." But then, you know, that's followed up by saying that Big Walk was developed "without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards." So, not to worry, they learned touching the stove is bad by touching the stove, and definitely won't do it again in future. If only there were thousands of other cases informing them why touching the stove is bad.

Very relevant to this reveal is the recent statement by select jurors of the Independent Games Festival which, after much internal deliberation, came to the conclusion that those who sign the statement would decline to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity, with signees including Austin Walker, Sam Barlow, Lena Reine, Brendon Chung, Aura Triolo, aurahack and more. The statement specifies that "AI-generated code is not an exception to these harms." Fellow juror Liz Ryerson confirmed that Big Walk was being considered by the IGF, and was a matter of discussion in judging as to whether its use of genAI would be acceptable.

As for House House only disclosing this now, they state it was not only because it was necessary for their IGF submission, but also that "we have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage", and that they have spoken on it publicly to Aftermath because "it has become a matter of public interest."

If I were to be cynical, I would say that House House would prefer to be the ones breaking this news themselves rather than having the IGF reveal that they had been hiding their use up until now; it's usually easier to control PR if you release it yourself. Big Walk had already been securely in everyone's good books for its support for the BDS boycott, for example, so why ruin that clean rep with something like a genAI disclosure?

I don't know how better to close this article than with an excerpt from that very IGF statement:

"We know that change does not come at the individual level, but as independent developers, we also know firsthand the value of pushing back on what an industry has deemed "inevitable." As jurists, we feel a responsibility to push past defeatism and aspire to a higher ideal.

The future is not yet settled. You are not alone. We can stand together."

#3971. Forza Horizon 6 Content Roadmap Revealed For Late 2026 & 2027

With a specific focus on January and February of next year

Ready for some more news on Forza Horizon 6? The team at Playground Games has announced a content roadmap for the game today, pulling the curtain back on their plans for the end of 2026 and all of next year.

You can get loads of detail about all of this in the video up above, but in a nutshell, we're getting Series 8 "Horizon Holidays" and Series 9 "Legendary Explorers" before the year is out. Then, as we head into January and February, Series 10 will be based around "Exotics and Tuners", while other new additions include a permanent new radio station, absolutely loads of new Reward Cars, and various other bits and bobs.

Most importantly, the first expansion for the game will also be released in January of 2027. Playground Games still doesn't want to talk about it just yet, but apparently we'll be hearing about it very soon.

News Forza Horizon 6's First Premium Expansion Planned For January 2027 Alongside PS5 Launch

Sony fans loved FH5, will they vibe with FH6? Probably

As you can see from the rest of this roadmap, the remainder of 2027 gets more vague for now, but it's confirmed that a second expansion is on the way along with a Festival Playlist overhaul, new race routes and various other new features.

They do talk quite a lot about the Festival Playlist overhaul in the video up above, so again, it's well worth a watch if you want to know more about what's on the way to Forza Horizon 6 in the future.

All of this sounds pretty good to us, and considering how the game has come in for a little bit of disgruntlement in recent months, it's clear to see that Playground Games is hoping for a strong 2027 when it comes to new FH6 content.

Avatar: Seven Havens season 2 has officially set its release date, and it's not too far away. The Legend of Korra sequel will release Book 2 on May 21, 2027.

Just like the first season, there will be 13 episodes in total, and they will air in three-episode chunks through to June 11. The next stage of Pavi and Nisha's journey is called 'Book Two: Discovery' and the synopsis teases plenty more adventure yet for the twins.

Speaking to GamesRadar+, executive producer Ethan Spaulding teased the show's new location in Book 2. "I'd say get your surfboards," he told us, suggesting a rewatch of the finale. "I think if you guys freeze-frame, you can kind of get a vibe of what that haven might be like. But yeah, it's a fun place."

Avatar: Seven Havens Book One is out now on Paramount Plus. For what else to watch, check out our guide to the best shows on Paramount Plus as well as our round-up of all the upcoming TV shows you need to know about.

VisionQuest's post-credits scene ups his appearance count

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Despite being a late addition swap-in as Marvel's big new villain, Doctor Doom has now had the same number of appearances as Thanos. Before 2018's Avengers: Infinity War, Thanos appeared in two end-credit scenes for The Avengers (2012) and Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015), as well as in the story of Guardians of the Galaxy (2015), all setting him up as the MCU's big bad.

Marvel hasn't had the same luxury of time with Doom, as one Twitter user pointed out, after he was announced in 2024 following Jonathan Majors being axed as Kang. As a result, the studio has been speedrunning his introduction, including him in three post-credits scenes in just over a year.

His first silent appearance came at the end of Fantastic Four: The First Steps in July 2025, when he's seen speaking to a young Franklin Richards before Sue Storm walks in. His second two appearances saw him recruiting new team members for his nefarious plans.

In Avengers: Endgame Encore, he finds Bruce Banner being held in a prison post-Spider-Man: Brand New Day before taking him away. His most shocking appearance then came at the end of VisionQuest, when he resurrects Scarlet Witch, telling her that her power will be his.

Doctor Doom now has the same number of appearances as Thanos had before Infinity War https://t.co/Wm1EibapW0November 11, 2026

It's been a pretty quick turnaround of set-up for Doom ahead of Doomsday, but it does mean we have some insight into what he's planning ahead of the movie's December release. It seems he's been recruiting several powerful figures to help in his fight against the Avengers.

Marvel fans have been reacting to the appearances, and it's fair to say that opinions are pretty mixed. "Thanos sent the army & Loki on Earth in 2012, & was the presence looming over the entire Guardians of The Galaxy AND there were a ton of people that were connected to him & suffered a lot because of him, seeking him," one wrote on Twitter, adding: "Btw I'm not saying this to trash Marvel with Doom, I can't wait for Doomsday, but yes, I wish they had him felt more to build up the DEPTH of the hype."

Meanwhile another wrote: "Honestly, they handled the switch from Kang to Doom really well, given the obvious reasons for it." A third then tweeted: "Imagine if Doom was planned from the start: his face with the hammer sound in Endgame (2019), Wanda in Doctor Strange (2022), Loki visiting Steve and the TVA’s fear in Loki's series, Bruce's kidnapping in Spider-Man BND, All set up years ago instead of added later."

Avengers: Doomsday hits UK cinemas on December 16 and US theaters on December 18. For more upcoming superhero movies, here's our guide to new Marvel movies and shows on the way.

#3968. Star Wars: Galactic Racer Reaches 1.5 Million Players, Teases Future Updates

Developer Fuse Games has announced its debut title, the brilliant Star Wars: Galactic Racer, has amassed 1.5 million players.

The news comes via a recent social post, featuring the one and only Biddy Blas himself:

It's unclear if the number equates with sales or is purely the number of people that have logged in, but either way, it's a pretty impressive milestone for the arcade racing title.

Galactic Racer has amassed this amount of players in a little over a month, when it launched to an overwhelmingly positive reception.

Its relentlessly fast racing, silky smooth controls, and moreish roguelike structure made it all stand out, and speaking personally, it's easily one of my favourite games of 2026. I wrote about it recently, and used it as an excuse to mention Burnout far too many times.

Anyway, the post also suggests the team is not done with Galactic Racer yet. Fuse Games says it "can't wait to share more about the future of Star Wars: Galactic Racer", which is a very exciting prospect.

Many are hopeful for additional locations and courses, even more abilities and perks for build variety, and features like creating custom events. I'd love for all of this to be added eventually, but for now we don't know exactly what the team's plans entail.

#3967. Following site-wide discussion on AI use, Nexus Mods add a "daily limit" to the spots in the new mods tab one person can hog via multiple rapid-fire uploads

It's a "stopgap solution" while the site's staff are busy "working on more sophisticated tools"

The folks behind Nexus Mods have rolled out a new "daily limit" system which ensures modders who upload multiple works in bulk during a single 24 hour period can't take up more than one spot in the tabs dedicated to showing off new mods for different games. Instead, those who chuck up their mods in bulk will see one of their works given a spot, while the rest are neatly filed away behind it, ready to spring out if you click a bit of text indicating that modder's got other fresh works to show off.

"Nexus Mods owner and CEO Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann hinted measures related to making the glut of new mods currently uploaded on a daily basis less of a discovery nightmare in last week's announcement post about the site's current policy regarding the use of genAI in mod making. "We’ve received feedback regarding authors uploading numerous mods at once and overwhelming the Recently Added section, pushing everyone else down the page," he wrote. "This is less of an issue related to AI, but it’s becoming much more prevalent as mod production is speeding up. Thus, we’re trying out limits on the number of mods from one author that can be shown in this section to give others a better chance of getting noticed. We’re also putting tighter restrictions on uploads from newly created accounts. The first of these updates will be available soon."

Cue an an announcement on Nexus Mods' Discord server yesterday by community manager Phoenix introducing the new "daily limit", which Nexus were keen to emphasise is "an experiment" they're open to feedback on. "We know that time in the New Mods view is important for a new mod to be discovered and we believe every mod author should have equal chances of having their work seen," they wrote. "While we're working on more sophisticated tools to give you control over the mods displayed to you, we are testing a stopgap solution that we hope will address the issue for now: For the time being, the New Mods view will display one mod per mod author. This limit refreshes every twenty-four hours – so if you publish one mod every day, you won't be affected."

The All Mods, Updated, Trending, Popular, and Surprise tabs for games are unaffected by the change, so will still dedicate a tab to each work regardless of who uploaded it when. If you take a glance at the New Mods pages for the likes of Skyrim, Fallout 4, and Cyberpunk 2077 this morning, you can already see the new mod stacking in action. The most mods from the same author I've seen stacked atop each other so far is 14 Fallout 4 works piled up.

It's worth noting you can also toggle the show only one new mod per modder rule off in the new mods tab, bringing back the older layout with one slot per mod regardless of uploader.

Personally, I tend to sort by mods with the most endorsements or downloads within the past 24 hours or seven days when I'm scanning for new mods, rather than just scrolling back through the new mods tab. Though I appreciate that could mean I've been missing out on some stellar works by lesser known modders whose creations never get the traction they merit thanks to being buried under an avalanche of other works. If so, hopefully this update does help the lone mods avoid being run over by mass upload freight trains.

#3966. Opinion: Nintendo Made Ocarina Of Time's Best Moment Even Better

Before launch, I didn't think it would be possible for anyone to spoil Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 for me.

I've played through the N64 original more times than I care to admit, and know it better than just about any other game out there. That said, if someone had told me about the Master Sword moment in the remake before I got to it, I would have been really upset.

And so, let's consider this a formal warning. If you haven't made it to the moment when Link first pulls the Master Sword from its Temple of Time pedestal in the Switch 2 remake yet, then stop reading right now and only return once you have seen it for yourself. It is spectacular, but it's something that warrants going in completely blind to really hit home. You have been warned.

You know what, I'm even going to stick a picture of Darunia below, just so that the coming paragraphs aren't spoiledFair does by an over-zealous scroll. This is your last chance to turn back!

Okay, all clear? Let's talk about how incredible the new Master Sword cutscene is.

This moment in the original is one of my foundational gaming memories. The score, the blue lighting, the threat of Ganondorf's giant looming face. It's all just chef's kiss levels of fantastic.

Knowing full well that my partner didn't know the mid-game twist — and desperate to show her the first walk out of the Temple of Time and the source of so much childhood trauma — I called her in and promised her a slice of "peak gaming". I thought we had seen almost all of its new form in the remake trailers.

But I was very wrong. Even in a game as well-known a quantity as this, Nintendo still had a surprise up its sleeve.

And so, we sat together as Link first pulled the Master Sword from the pedestal. I had a little cry as he swung the sword around, and I was ready to move straight to the Chamber of Sages lore dump. What I didn't expect was a full-blown cinematic from the gates of the Sacred Realm, some bonus Ganondorf content, and an image so threatening that it definitely would have given me nightmares for weeks had it been in the original.

I'm talking about rocky Link, petrified with the Master Sword in hand as Ganondorf taunts him while sauntering his way to the Triforce.

It follows the already stunning image of Link opening the door to the Sacred Realm itself, awash with dreamy lighting and colouring, making the pivot to dread all the more impactful. I'm a particular fan of the Ganondorf motif sting right as Link turns to stone. It's all so chilling!

I was seeing one of my most-replayed games from a new perspective.

What a fantastic surprise, as well. I've loved all of the little extra cutscenes in the remake and the bonus context they provide (a particular shoutout to the Kokiri watching the Great Deku Tree's leaves fall), but this one felt like the first moment that I was seeing one of my most-replayed games from a new perspective. My imagination had filled in Ganondorf's menace and Link's helplessness in the N64 original, but never quite like this.

It was made all the more special to be watching it with someone who had no idea what was coming next. While I gasped and cried at seeing images that I had only ever imagined, she did the same, witnessing all the drama for the first time. Honestly, there's nothing quite like seeing someone's jaw drop at their first realisation of the time jump.

Such a special moment is carried into its follow-up scene. After returning to the Temple of Time and meeting Sheik, you walk into Hyrule as you now find it, destroyed and crumbling at the hands of Ganondorf.

While there's something innately unsettling about the N64's handling of this moment (the silence of the Temple courtyard contrasted with the first scream of a ReDead is wonderful), the remaster dedicates another short cutscene to highlighting everything that's gone wrong.

Panning over the decimated rooftops to Ganon's Castle in the distance, it really showcases just how broken the world has become in Link's seven years away. There's an argument to be made that everything is more sinister if you're forced to imagine it (look at how scary Jaws is before you see the shark), but man, what a feeling it is to finally see it realised after decades of keeping it in my head.

The remake isn't something that I want to rush, so I'm making sure that I go slow. I still have some of my favourite temples, bosses and puzzles to come, but if this is how it handles my favourite moment in the game (maybe in all of gaming), then I'm going to need to buy another box of tissues.

What do you make of the new Master Sword moment in Ocarina of Time? Let us know in the comments.

The original is clearly a masterpiece, but it always felt like... a playable stage play? Or reading a book where you already know all the key plot points through cultural osmosis? It never felt like a special, personal experience for me.

The remake completely changes that. Now it's deeply personal, extremely moving. It's amazing what a new art direction, set dressings, musical score, some extra dialog, and a few more small cutscenes in key moments can do.

It's still the same underlying game, but it hits so much harder. The way you can see the Deku Tree looming over the forest village in the beginning, and then the cutscene after you finish the first child dungeon... You really feel the effect that moment has on the Kokiri.

Or even the redesigned entrance to the ice cavern. Where before it was some generic looking cave you stumble upon, now it really looks and feels like the source of the freeze - from the snowy wind to the imposing entrance to the cavern, like everything in the area is visually drawing you toward that entrance now.

So many little things that are executed perfectly and add up to make this game an emotional experience like it never was before. Characters feel like real people with lives and desires rather than pawns in a larger plot. All it takes is a few more facial animations, lines of dialog reacting to events, and better camera angles and lighting during pivotal moments.

Oh and last thing, holy crap does each dungeon feel like a unique place, a real location that means something to the surrounding area - each one having its own music (as it did in the original) and enhanced so much visually in this remake to really set them apart, it provides such a stark contrast to the more generic shrines and such from BotW/TotK. It shows how great the classic Zelda formula can really be with modern technology and care put into each location.

They really mastered the nostalgia and classic moments while making it feel new for longtime players who have torn Hyrule apart for all it's secrets and hundreds of hours of gameplay

#3965. PSA: Xbox And GTA 6 Have Both Pushed Out Small New Updates

One's a console update, the other potentially a "day one" patch

As we get ready to wrap up the working week here at Pure Xbox, we wanted to alert you to a couple of new updates that have been pushed out in recent days - one for Xbox consoles in general, and another specifically for GTA 6.

The Xbox console update was actually released on Wednesday, but nobody made a song and dance about it whatsoever, while the patch notes only referenced "general stability and performance improvements".

However, we now know that the update was related to the addition of achievements in four original Xbox games, and unless you download the update, you won't be able to see those achievements right now.

There's a chance your console may have downloaded this automatically but to check, go to "Settings", "System", "Updates" and then see if there's an update waiting to be downloaded or not.

News Four OG Xbox Games Are Getting Achievements For The First Time Ever

"We’re introducing one of the top requested features"

As for GTA 6, in addition to the 200GB+ preload that went live a few days ago, there's also now a new update as of a few hours ago that sits at around 2.2GB. You'll need to download this in order to start playing on November 19th.

Some people are speculating that this might be the so-called "day one patch", but who knows whether we might get another one between now and next Thursday. In any case, you'll want to get this queued up as soon as possible (unless you haven't installed the game yet, in which case it'll be included in your initial download).

There's a chance you may see a different size, but it's somewhere around that 2.2GB mark. We're also spotting that some people haven't got it yet for whatever reason, but it should roll out to all Xbox users in the very near future.

Don't forget that Alpha Skip-Ahead Xbox Insiders have also received a special new update this week that adds three new features for testing purposes, so if you're part of the Insider programme, keep an eye out for that.

We'll be back next week with loads more coverage on the GTA 6 launch, and here's hoping there are no more downloads to get us ready for November 19th. Just a few more sleeps until the big day!

#3964. Kevin Feige didn't want Wanda Maximoff to reunite with Vision in VisionQuest because the show should "stand on its own"

Paul Bettany says they considered bringing Wanda back

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

VisionQuest came to a close with an epic season finale that saw Vision reunite with both of his sons, Billy and Tommy Maximoff. However, there was a missing member of the family: Wanda Maximoff. She's mentioned several times in the final few episodes but doesn't appear in the main series.

However, it turns out that they did consider bringing her back. Speaking to The Playlist, Vision star Paul Bettany said: "I remember having this conversation with [Kevin Feige], and he said, 'You and Terry [Matalas, showrunner] have done such a great job at making me care about Vision. I really don't think you should distract from that by giving the audience that at the end of the [show]. It will just fundamentally all become about WandaVision again, and this should and can stand on its own.' And I think he was right."

Of course, this doesn't mean that Wanda doesn't appear at all in the Disney Plus show. In the finale's second post-credits scene, Doctor Doom takes a trip to Mount Wundagore. We see Wanda pull down the mountain on top of her, as happened in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, before Doom appears and lifts the stones off of her. He brings her back to life before saying, "Scarlet Witch awaken, your power will be mine."

Elizabeth Olsen looks set to appear in Avengers: Doomsday then and a recent leak from Anthony Mackie seemed to confirm that Vision is coming back too. We may finally get a Maximoff reunion after all then, although probably not under the best of circumstances.

#3963. Skydance Games lay off an undisclosed number of staff in the wake of Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, in latest case of consolidation killing livelihoods

A little over a month following the huge, vile, culture-defining (negative) merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. into Skydance, the corporation has confirmed that games division Skydance Games will be facing a round of layoffs, according to a report from Variety.

Skydance Games was born from combining Paramount and Warner Bros' own individual divisions, bringing developers like NetherRealm, Rocksteady, WB Games Montreal/Boston, TT Games and Avalanche under the same umbrella as Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra developers and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin publishers Paramount Games Studio. All this was was done, of course, to maximise the amount of IP that the corporation can access to base games on, such as Avatar: The Last Airbender, Game of Thrones, Star Trek, the DC Universe, Harry Potter, and more. Skydance Games came into existence on October 6th; it barely lasted a month as it was.

In a statement given to Variety, Skydance confirmed that "As part of our ongoing efforts to position Skydance Games for long-term growth and success, we are implementing reorganization and operational shifts across a few areas of our business. We have stepped back and taken some time to consider where we are investing our efforts and have made the difficult decision to scale down some of our projects. As a result, there are roles impacted. This is not a reflection of the talent, dedication, or creativity of those affected and we are grateful for their contributions. We are committed to approaching the process with transparency, care and respect for those who are leaving the company." Skydance did not disclose the number of staff affected.

Skydance joins the ever-growing list of corporations that have mandated layoffs in the recent past, such as Microsoft, Ubisoft, and EA. Workers will bleed until there is no one left to cut. Solidarity to all affected.

#3961. Mini Review: Tape To Tape (Switch) - A Great Roguelite For Underserved Hockey Lovers

If you are a hockey fan with a Switch, you have been poorly served by the system’s library. Odd really, considering how well hockey itself translates into video game form. And then you chance upon Tape to Tape drowning in the weekly AI slop eShop releases, a curiously labelled “gorgeous roguelite hockey world" affair. Is this it? Is this the hockey game of my dreams?

Tape to Tape did not sprout magically overnight. It has been a labour of love for several years and has been feeding off a lively player community with feedback to shape the version now in our hands. Forget about offsides, penalties, and other obtuse rules (unless you pick the Modern Squad): this is hardcore old-school hockey the likes of which we haven't seen since NHL Hitz and that is a very good thing indeed.

While this is strictly an offline couch multiplayer affair with all the expected gameplay modes up to four players, the real meat is found in the campaign mode, where its roguelite nature shines. You start with a choice of three teams, with another 16 unlocking as you make progress and meet unlock conditions. Each comes with their own gameplay quirks, with some being significant advantages while others rapidly become heavy handicaps.

In my dozen or so (not all of them successful) runs, there were no two alike, thanks to the sizeable amount of possible combos of team, star players, bench-warmers, unlockable team relics, and individual player skills. A successful run will expose huge chunks of delightfully silly lore and can run to over an hour while you pick your path between opponents' stadiums and a cast of oddball individuals that will (mostly) help to bring out your team's potential.

The other unexpected stars are the opponent teams, from stereotypical spoofs like the soccer team (with easily recognisable caricatures of real-life players) that doesn’t even use sticks to play to the Canadian team that requires tariffs (translating into huge handicaps per period) and has their heads animated in unmistakable South Park fashion, all the way up to the hockey nemesis themselves, the club wielding Golfers in the final campaign act.

And the less said about the cheating Officials team, the better. Having a clean run end abruptly because the official grabs the puck and shoves it into the back of your net might be part of the fun, but it still stings.

Overall, this is a refreshingly addictive take on hockey, with tight gameplay, humour that lands, and rewarding unlockable content. The Switch edition offers something not found on other versions: the option to throw a Joy-Con at other players and have a quick match in tabletop mode. If you grew up with Ice Hockey and Blades of Steel on NES, Mutant League Hockey on Mega Drive, and the all-mighty, all-conquering NHL Hitz on sixth-generation hardware, this game was made for you.

If you have never played a hockey game in your life before and have zero interest in the sport, this game is also for you! Tape to Tape is not just a great hockey video game - it is a great video game, period.

#3960. Talking Point: What Are You Playing This Weekend? (November 14-15)

It's the penultimate weekend to get stuck into the games you'd like to finish before November 19th rolls up.

It's WAYP time, people! You know the score by now, so let's hear what you're playing this weekend! This is your opportunity to have a chat with one another about what's good, what's worth playing, why you're vibing, or maybe, not vibing with certain games. It's an open floor, PX'ers.

Alrighty then, let's get into it. Here's what we're playing on Xbox this weekend:

Recently, I haven't been trying to complete anything, grind online, or chase a Mythic cheevo. I'm just vibing with my Xbox. Honestly, I think GTA 6 has me in a bit of a chokehold, keeping me from starting anything I might not finish. With that in mind, Hozy has been the perfect lil' game to sit down and chill with on a rainy day.

Lots of games are getting little bits of my attention, including Silver Pines, TCG Card Shop Simulator, and Gears of War: E-Day, to name a few. But, my main game at the moment is It Takes Two. I've absolutely loved playing it with my wife. The best bit is how into it she is, that and the bonded trauma it inflicts!

Something I'd like to get back into is Marathon. That new Symbiosis trailer looked awesome, and I'm hoping to lock-in and get that Mythic. I think all I need is to grind to level 100 and it'll be mine. Shouldn't be too much of a time commitment, right?

But I'll be real. I'm playing a lot of Zelda: Ocarina of Time right now. It's a perfect remake of a childhood favourite, and it's feeding my inner kid. He's a happy boy.

GTA 6 is right around the corner, and you better believe it's going to take up the rest of the year in terms of dominating my free time. That means it's not really wise to get stuck into anything too meaty right now, although I'm keen to check out Shrek 2 Remastered and see whether Aspyr's new port does the OG Xbox title justice or not.

I might even play a bit of GTA: Chinatown Wars on my 3DS. I finally started playing that game about a year ago, and even though it's rough around the edges by today's standards, I'm enjoying how unique it is compared to other entries.

#3959. The Game Awards 2026 Nominees to Be Revealed on 17th November

Geoff Keighley has announced the nominees for all of the categories at The Game Awards will be confirmed next week, on 17th November 2026.

A livestream will confirm the game's nominated, with the show itself airing on 10th December 2026. You can tune in for the nominee livestream at 9am PT / 12pm ET / 5pm GMT.

Obviously, the question now becomes: what games will be in contention for Game of the Year?

It's confirmed that GTA 6 will be eligible for all the awards, despite the fact the game won't launch until two days after it could be nominated for the top accolade. I personally believe, with complete confidence, it will be nominated for Game of the Year, but we'll have to see what happens during the livestream next week.

Six games compete for Game of the Year, so what could join it? The likes of Resident Evil Requiem, 007 First Light, and Big Walk all seem like obvious contenders. Other potential inclusions could be Control Resonant, Phantom Blade Zero, or The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — depending on how the jury feels about including remakes.

All will be revealed on Tuesday, 17th November 2026. What games do you want to see nominated? Post your pick in the comments below.

#3958. Steam's new Steam Deck framerate graphs are good news for handheld players, though I wouldn't fully trust the numbers yet

Valve have finally made clear what they've been doing with all that hoovered-up performance data and all those "Framerate Estimator" text strings: a framerate estimator for the Steam Deck. Or, rather, a framerate average-r, as games on the Steam Store are now getting attached graphs – under their existing Steam Deck Compatibility details – that show how many frames-per-secondseses that game has been recording on real players' handhelds, the OLED and original LCD models both.

The thinking, as Valve explain in a Steam post, is to set more precise performance expectations than the existing verification ratings – Verified, Playable, and Unsupported – provide. This may induce some gentle learned nodding, if you've ever tried an Unsupported game only to find it works more or less fine, or have ever wondered why a game that can just about scrape 30fps together gets the same green good-job sticker as something that screams along at 90fps. Now, when checking that rating, you'll also get a relatively specific idea of smoothness and/or chugging potential.

Or will you? By Valve's own admission, the displayed results may be skewed by V-Sync treachery, where this anti-screen tear setting (which many games enable by default) could force games into briefly running at unrepresentative framerates. The scoundrel. My current handheld game beau, Mortal Shell II, looks like it may be falling victim to this: its results for the LCD Steam Deck show it mostly runs around 30fps, which is in line with my experience, but the OLED results show it averaging around 45fps. The Steam Deck OLED's APU is a tiny bit quicker than the LCD Deck's, but it's not that much of an upgrade.

There's work to be done, then, though I do appreciate the concept. As tightly as I cling to my battery-efficient, mercifully Windows-free Deck OLED in the face of drastically more powerful handhelds, with every year it becomes a little less likely that new games will comfortably run on it. Verification ratings can still act as decent (if broad) guidelines, but even with V-Sync putting an immaculately untorn thumb on the scales, game-specific framerate data will be much more illustrative.

As for whether these histograms will also get Steam Machine versions, or perhaps cover non-Valve handhelds, Valve say this: "We see this update as a stepping stone toward providing framerate data for more devices than just Steam Deck. To this end, we are also prompting customers to opt-in to providing anonymized framerate data in the Steam desktop client. This opt-in is currently only on Steam Client Beta, and will ship to all customers in the future." So, maybe, if you gizzus yer data.

Marvel fans think a Deadpool cameo could be on the cards after Ryan Reynolds responds to his Avengers: Doomsday writing credit in the most cryptic way

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

In a bizarre turn of events, it looks like Ryan Reynolds has a writing credit on Avengers: Doomsday, but the Deadpool star has replied in the most hilarious yet confusing way.

One eagle-eyed Marvel fan spotted Reynolds' name under Doomsday's screenwriting credits on the Writers Guild of America’s directory and shared a screenshot of the listing on Twitter. But in true Deadpool fashion, Reynolds hasn't confirmed whether he did pen part of the Marvel movie. Instead, the actor responded with a clip from Deadpool and Wolverine, where the mutant says, "Not to brag, but I do not read." Check out the post below.

It is true that both Reynolds and his Deadpool 3 co-star Hugh Jackman are both listed among the various other writers who worked on the movie, which also includes Spider-Man: Brand New Day director Destin Daniel Cretton. Though this marks Jackman's first Marvel writing credit, this wouldn't be the first time Reynolds has chipped in on a script, as the star was also one of the writers on Deadpool 2 and his 2024 MCU debut, Deadpool & Wolverine.

Reynolds' response is rather confusing, but Marvel fans are taking that Deadpool "can't read" as a sign that he didn't pen the script, but is rather in the movie. "Deadpool in Avengers: Doomsday confirmed!?" said one fan, and another added, "Little Doomsey is going to shit himself when he sees the boys walk up on him."

As far as we know, Reynolds and Jackman have not been cast in Avengers: Doomsday. However, it is not entirely impossible. Despite announcing the bulk of the cast during the unforgettable Avengers: Doomsday livestream event, co-director Anthony Russo has confirmed that he and Joe Russo still haven't announced the full cast.

Fans have been wondering whether Jackman's Wolverine will join his fellow mutants, as most of the original Fox-era X-Men are coming back, including Patrick Stewart's Charles Xavier, Ian McKellen's Magneto, James Marsden's Cyclops, and more. But with just one month before the movie hits screens, we would guess that any more major reveals may be saved for the big day.

Avengers: Doomsday hits cinemas on December 18, and December 16 in the UK. For more, check out our guide to the Marvel timeline, and keep up with upcoming Marvel movies and shows on the way.

#3956. Take-Two boss isn't ruling out a GTA movie or TV show, but says they're "very, very selective" about who they work with

A Grand Theft Auto movie could still happen one day

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

With less than a week to go until the release of GTA 6 – aka the biggest entertainment release of all time – the boss of GTA publisher Take-Two isn't ruling out a GTA movie or TV show, but suggests one hasn't happened yet because they're "very, very selective" about who they work with.

Speaking on The David Rubenstein Show, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked why, after 30 years and six mainline games, there still hasn't been a GTA adaptation, saying in response: "We're very careful about line extensions [adaptations in other mediums] because this is a creative company and our goal is to make the best entertainment on Earth.

"We would make a movie or a television show based on our IP if our creative teams were passionate about it," Zelnick continued. "If they thought that would somehow engage and delight our consumers. It's a high bar to do that, and of course there's always the risk of failure. So we don't rule it out, but we're very, very selective."

Video game adaptations are currently all the rage in Hollywood. 2026 alone saw the release of Resident Evil, Mortal Kombat 2, Street Fighter, Iron Lung, Exit 8, Return to Silent Hill, and the back half of Fallout season 2, and 2027 looks to be even bigger for video games on screen with The Legend of Zelda movie, A Minecraft Movie 2, Sonic 4, and potentially a wave of TV shows set to release. GTA is a unique case, however, and given its scale, it's arguable that Rockstar and Take-Two would have more to lose than gain from a GTA movie or TV show if any adaptation can't live up to the medium-defining legacy of the games.

That said, imagine a GTA movie directed by one of the crime movie greats – a Michael Mann or a Martin Scorsese. Could Rockstar resist if one of the legendary filmmakers who informed much of their work wanted to return the favor? For now, the closest we have to a GTA movie is the 2015 docudrama The Gamechangers, which stars Harry Potter's Daniel Radcliffe as then Rockstar Games President Sam Houser and depicts the legal battle with Florida attorney Jack Thompson over the supposed psychological effects of violent games. Rockstar, famously, weren't fans, tweeting: "Was Basil Brush busy? What exactly is this random, made-up bollocks?"

As for GTA 6, the map for the long-awaited Vice City-set game just leaked, and it could be teasing a UFO Easter egg. For that and much more, head on over to our countdown to GTA 6 landing page.

GTA 6 releases on November 19. For more, check out our list of the best video game movies, and our guide to all the upcoming video game movies and shows heading our way.

#3954. Tripwire Interactive says it's laying off 36 staff in a "necessary" decision, while reassuring that Killing Floor 3 and Maneater 2 are still in active development

In a statement posted yesterday, Killing Floor developers Tripwire Interactive have announced that the studio is laying off 36 "talented" internal staff as part of a "workforce reduction". The job cuts come 16 months after the release of Killing Floor 3 (which James didn't care for), and within hours of unrelated yet equally dispiriting redunancies at Skydance Games.

Tripwire's announcement claims that this was "not an easy decision, but unfortunately a necessary one for the organisation," adding that "these are truly great people who are exceptional at their roles, and we will help support these individuals with compassion and dignity during this transition." There's a small hope in me that this might mean helping those affected find new jobs quickly, though it's hard to stay optimistic when mass layoffs in games development have become such a regular occurrence.

Despite this post primarily being about the loss of 36 livelihoods, Tripwire are quick to reassure fans that Killing Floor 3's post-launch updates remain in active development, as does their comedy shark-action sequel Maneater 2. The studio "remain committed to our awesome community", they say; apparently just not to their awesome employees.

This news also arrives just days after Tripwire expanded its publishing business to support small indie developers, and less than a year after its last round of layoffs in March. Tripwire also happens to have been acquired by layoff extraordinaire corporation Embracer in 2022, just for some relevant context.

#3953. Minecraft Is Getting Joy-Con Mouse Controls On Switch 2 In A Future Update

You can try them out now in the closed beta

If you've read our Minecraft Switch 2 review here on Nintendo Life, you'll know one thing currently missing from this version is mouse mode.

Fortunately, an update is already in the works to add Joy-Con 2 mouse controls to this version of the game. These controls can be accessed right now in the closed beta build.

This includes the ability to use mouse controls with either the left or right Joy-Con, and you can also customise settings, such as cursor and camera sensitivity. Additionally, you place blocks with the 'ZL' button, and break and select blocks with the 'ZR' button. Button layout can also be adjusted in the game's settings.

At the moment, there's no release date for the official rollout of mouse controls on Switch 2, but they'll be made available to every player at some point in the future.

In case you missed it, Minecraft players who own a digital Switch copy of the game can currently get a free Switch 2 upgrade until the end of January 2027. Owners of a physical copy on Switch can also get a discount on the Minecraft 'Ultimate Collection' upgrade for Switch 2.
